messages:
anya: Quick follow-up on hosting/dedicated/private surface — can we agree on a single 'capability vector' proto instead of separate manifests? Thinking operational clarity + easier rollbacks.

mike: +1 on the idea in principle. Main worry is the explosion of optional fields and vendor-specific knobs.

priya: Could be fine if we keep it strictly additive and versioned. We had the same issue with routing policies earlier.

lucas: My wildcard: how do we express 'eviction and affinity' semantics across modes? Hosted needs soft-evict, private needs admin-evict, dedicated has quotas. Those feel orthogonal to capabilities.

anya: Good catch. Proposal: split the proto into two logical groups: 1) declarative capability vector (model features, streaming, kv-cache, quantization tiers) and 2) runtime policy bundle (eviction, affinity, SLA class, fallback order). Both packaged together but semantically separated.

ashley: That maps nicely to ops. We can let Dedicated/Private provide stricter policy overrides. But how do we enforce compatibility at runtime?

priya: Add a lightweight compatibility check step in control-plane that validates the capability vector against runtime capabilities before pinning. If mismatch, return a structured error with suggested fallbacks.

mike: We should also keep a 'graceful-degradation' map in the proto: if feature X missing, fallback to Y. Avoid hard failures in hosted when dedicated variant not available.

anya: Exactly. Example snippet: ```proto
message CapabilityVector {
  repeated string features = 1; // e.g. "streaming", "kv_cache"
  map<string,string> quality_tiers = 2; // latency -> "low"/"best"
  RuntimePolicy policy = 3;
}
message RuntimePolicy {
  enum Eviction { SOFT=0; HARD=1; ADMIN=2; }
  Eviction eviction = 1;
  repeated string fallback_order = 2;
}
```

lucas: Love the example. Action item: prove out the compatibility check as a small endpoint in control-plane. If it can catch simple mismatches (quantization not supported on that runtime), it's already valuable.

ashley: Ops needs the audit trail: when control-plane rewrites policy (e.g., adds a fallback), we must persist the original and the delta. Prefer immutable records per deploy.

priya: Agreed — add a `provenance` field with `original_spec` and `applied_overrides` (hash refs) so we can audit and roll back.

mike: One more tradeoff: single proto simplifies tooling, but increases blast radius for schema changes. We should attach strict major/minor versioning and an automatic compatibility linter in CI.

anya: Totally. Proposed governance: any non-backwards-compatible change requires an RFC + migration plan + canary window. We already do this, but call it out for the capability proto.

ashley: For Dedicated customers, we must allow silent local overrides (on-prem operator wants full control). How does that interact with pinning?

priya: Override precedence: local operator > customer control-plane > Redwood default. Documented and surfaced in Console. If local override exists, the compatibility check should run against the resolved runtime stack.

lucas: Edge-case: what if override enables a feature that the client SDK expects but hosted fallback can't emulate? We'll need runtime-level feature flags and an explicit 'client contract' that the API promises.

anya: Good point. Add `client_contract_version` and `exposed_features` for each served endpoint so SDK behavior remains deterministic.

infra-bot: deploybot: New CI job suggestion recorded: `capproto-lint` to run schema compatibility checks.

mike: Next steps: 1) Priya to draft the proto + sample mapping doc; 2) Lucas to prototype control-plane compatibility endpoint; 3) Ashley to write audit persistence sketch; 4) Anya to add governance checklist to RFC.

priya: I'll drop a first draft by EOD tomorrow. Will include examples for fallback_order semantics and minimal/strict validation modes.

lucas: I'll spike the endpoint this week — aiming to return `OK | WARN(suggested_fallbacks) | ERROR(reason)` JSON.

ashley: I'll outline the immutable record format and retention policy. Ops wants 90 days as a minimum.

anya: Thanks team. If we can keep this initial proto narrow (features + runtime policy + provenance + contract_version) we'll avoid scope creep. Will follow up with RFC update. :thumbsup:

mike: One tiny UX ask — Console should show the human-readable effective policy and the original spec diff. If we lose visibility, support tickets will blow up.

priya: noted. Will add spec->effective diff sample to the draft.

anya: Closing — will spin RFC draft after we get the proto skeleton. Re-open thread if blockers appear.

infra-bot: reminder: #arch-review meeting on Tue 10:30am — put this as a 5-min demo on the agenda.
